title: Range of the noised restriction endpoints
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ take values in $[0,1]$. Suppose $0\le\rho\le1$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. If $a_f$ is the average of the two restrictions of $f$ to the last coordinate and $d_f$ is their half-difference, then both $(T_\rho a_f)(x)+(T_\rho d_f)(x)$ and $(T_\rho a_f)(x)-(T_\rho d_f)(x)$ belong to $[0,1]$.
replaced: Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and let $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$. If $f$ takes values in $[0,1]$ and $0\le\rho\le1$, then $(T_\rho a_f)(x)\pm(T_\rho d_f)(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x$.
